Minnie Baldock Street

Named after suffragette Minnie Baldock. She co-founded the first branch of the Women’s Social and Political Union. After working in a sweated shirt factory most of her life she joined the socialist party in 1892 called the Independent Labour Party. Even though women weren’t allowed to be MPs at the time she was chosen by the party to sit on the West Ham Board of Guardians in 1905

Maud Road

Maud of Wales was Queen of Norway as the wife of King Haakon VII. She was the youngest daughter of Edward VII and Queen Alexandra of the United Kingdom. She was the first queen of an independent Norway in 500 years, she was known for her dedicated charity work.

Eleanor Road

Named after Eleanor Marx youngest daughter of Karl Marx. She herself was also a socialist who worked towards the liberation of the working class and women. She was the heart of the early trade union movement. She lived most her life in East London

Katherine Road

Named after Katherine Fry, daughter of philanthropist and prison reformer Elizabeth Fry. Elizabeth Road is off Katherine Road opposite Milton Avenue and Fry Road runs between Elizabeth Road and Phashet Grove. Katherine Fry wrote a number of books including A History of Parishes of East and West Ham.

Anna Neagle Close

Anna Neagle Close, Forest Gate was popular on both the stage and screen, Anna Neagle caught the eye of film producer Herbert Wilcox later to become her husband while performing in the West End in 1931. Her first film was a box office hit and by the late 1940s, she had become the most in demand British film actress. She continued to perform up to her death in 1986, aged 81..

Elizabeth Road

Elizabeth Fry, sometimes referred to as Betsy Fry, was an English prison reformer, social reformer, philanthropist and Quaker. Fry was a major driving force behind new legislation to improve the treatment of prisoners, especially female inmates, and as such has been called the 'Angel of Prisons.'
